risk_if_not_implemented: Without Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Automation, control validation remains manual, infrequent and error-prone, so control failures may go undetected between assessment cycles and reported control status may not reflect reality. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM)
compensating_control_1.description: Automated mechanisms exist to perform Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) to assess and report the conformity status of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) against applicable security, compliance and resilience controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) (CPL-18) compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Automation (IAO-15) by providing ongoing, semi-automated visibility into control status, which narrows the detection gap that fully automated Control Validation Testing (CVT) would otherwise close. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Control Validation Testing (CVT)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to formally assess the security, compliance and resilience controls in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting expected requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification: Control Validation Testing (CVT) (IAO-04) compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Automation (IAO-15) by performing periodic manual Control Validation Testing (CVT), which delivers the same assurance outcome at lower frequency and with greater reliance on assessor judgment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
